world.description: a pencil logistics and supply network

world.label: Pencil Supply Network
world.summary: Specialists produce, move, and sell pencils through a recurring supply network.

actions.description: Harvest logs from the managed forest.
Cut logs into wood slats at the sawmill.
Prepare graphite cores at the core workshop.
Assemble pencils from wood slats and graphite cores.
Deliver pencil stock from the factory to the stationery shop.
Sell pencils from the stationery shop to customers with waiting orders.

mechanics.rationale: The forester harvests logs from the chosen forest source, transferring the requested quantity into the forester's stock.
limits: Only a forester with the represented timber-harvesting role can harvest.
Harvesting fails if the selected forest lacks the requested logs.
tests: A forester can harvest a positive quantity that is available in a forest; the forest loses that quantity and the forester gains it.
The action is refused for a non-forester, a non-forest source, a nonpositive quantity, or insufficient forest logs.
semantic_bindings: quantity is the number of logs harvested

mechanics.rationale: The sawyer consumes logs available at the chosen sawmill and produces an equal quantity of wood slats there.
limits: Only a sawyer with the represented wood-slats role can cut logs.
Cutting fails when the sawmill lacks the requested logs.
tests: A sawyer can convert available sawmill logs to an equal quantity of slats.
The action is refused for a non-sawyer, a non-sawmill, a nonpositive quantity, or insufficient logs.
semantic_bindings: mill is the sawmill where the logs are cut
quantity is the number of logs cut and slats produced

mechanics.rationale: The miner gathers graphite from the selected mine, transferring the requested quantity into the miner's stock.
limits: Only a miner with the represented graphite-mining role can mine.
Mining fails if the selected mine lacks the requested graphite.
tests: A miner can gather available graphite; the mine loses the quantity and the miner gains it.
The action is refused for a non-miner, a non-mine source, a nonpositive quantity, or insufficient graphite.
semantic_bindings: quantity is the amount of graphite mined

mechanics.rationale: The core maker consumes graphite at the selected workshop and produces the same quantity of graphite cores there.

checks.label: The core maker makes graphite cores

limits: Only a core maker with the represented role can prepare cores.
Core-making fails when the workshop lacks the requested graphite.
tests: A core maker can convert available workshop graphite into an equal number of cores.
The action is refused for a non-core-maker, a non-workshop, a nonpositive quantity, or insufficient graphite.
semantic_bindings: workshop is the graphite core workshop
quantity is the amount of graphite consumed and cores produced

mechanics.rationale: The pencil maker consumes equal quantities of wood slats and graphite cores at the selected factory and produces pencils.

checks.label: The factory has enough wood slats
The factory has enough graphite cores

limits: Only a pencil maker with the represented assembly role can assemble pencils.
Assembly fails unless the factory has enough of both required inputs.
tests: A pencil maker can consume equal available quantities of slats and cores to produce pencils.
The action is refused for a non-pencil-maker, a non-factory, a nonpositive quantity, or insufficient input stock.
semantic_bindings: quantity is the number of pencils assembled and the amount of each input consumed

mechanics.rationale: The carrier moves pencil stock from the selected factory into the selected shop, subtracting it from the source and adding it to the destination.

checks.label: The factory and shop are different places

limits: Only a carrier with the represented pencil-moving role can deliver.
Delivery fails if the source lacks the requested pencils or the source and destination are the same entity.
tests: A carrier can deliver available pencils from a factory to a shop; the source loses and the shop gains the quantity.
The action is refused for a non-carrier, a non-factory source, a non-shop destination, a nonpositive quantity, insufficient stock, or identical endpoints.
semantic_bindings: source is the factory holding pencil stock
to is the stationery shop receiving pencil stock
quantity is the number of pencils delivered

mechanics.rationale: The shopkeeper serves a waiting order by removing the sold pencils and one waiting order from the shop, and replenishes customer demand to represent recurring orders.

checks.label: The shop has a waiting order

limits: Only a shopkeeper with the represented customer-serving role can serve an order.
Serving fails if the shop lacks pencils or has no waiting order.
Demand is represented at the customer entity; this action does not transfer pencil stock out of the shop because the action participants do not include the shop.
tests: The action is refused when the customer entity has no pencils or no waiting orders.
The action requires a positive quantity and the represented shopkeeper role.
semantic_bindings: customer represents the waiting customer orders and, as modeled here, the shop stock is not separately represented among the action participants
quantity is the number of pencils sold

processes.rationale: The managed forest replenishes its represented log resource over time, sustaining timber harvesting.
The represented graphite deposit replenishes gradually so mining can recur.
Logs are replenished at the sawmill to provide the next production step with recurring inputs.
Graphite is replenished at the core workshop so core-making can continue independently of transport actions not represented in this action set.
The factory receives recurring represented wood slat and graphite core inputs so pencil assembly remains actionable.
Customers continue to place orders, keeping shop demand recurring.

readout.title: How coordination slowed (the four mechanisms of the Waltzman paper)
readout.summary: The forester, miner, core-maker, sawyer, pencil-maker, and carrier repeatedly gathered materials, made pencils, and delivered them to the stationery shop. The shop’s pencil stock and waiting orders grew; the events show no coordination dispute or decision delay.

mechanisms.name: Reopened settled issues
mechanisms.missing_reason: No previously settled item is recorded as reopened.
